content_preview.title: Valve Funds Collabora's Port of Mesa's Open-Source RADV Vulkan Driver to Windows
content_preview.summary: Collabora, sponsored by Valve, has an experimental Windows build of Mesa's open-source RADV Vulkan driver running Counter-Strike 2, though it isn't Vulkan-conformant yet.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Collabora, the open-source engineering firm that maintains large parts of the Mesa graphics stack, has an experimental Windows build of RADV — Mesa's open-source Vulkan driver for AMD graphics hardware — running well enough to launch Counter-Strike 2, according to [Collabora](https://www.collabora.com/news-and-blog/news-and-events/cracking-windows-open-porting-radv-to-win32.html) and [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/valve-backs-radv-vulkan-driver-port-to-windows/). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category article (670 words), neutral tone, appropriate technical depth on the RADV-to-Windows port. No AI self-reference, no sensationalism.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 source snapshots read and sha256-verified against manifest.json in sources/2026-08/valve-funds-collaboras-port-of-mesas-open-source-radv-vulkan-driver-to-windows/: source-0.html.gz (Collabora blog, matches sha256 b62e6023...) confirms the 'Thanks also to Valve for sponsoring this phase of our work to bring open drivers to Windows' quote verbatim, the XDC 2024 / Faith Ekstrand / wddm2-pdd-re history, the RX 7900 XT vs RX 7800 XT hang issue, the MSVC enum-signedness bug, the D3DKMTEscape private-data risk, and the '3x performance gain for applications that are not GPU-bound' quote verbatim. source-1.html.gz (Linuxiac) confirms 'de facto Vulkan driver for AMD GPUs on Linux', the -vulkan command-line launch of Counter-Strike 2, and the 'sparse bindings, tessellation, task shaders, and dynamic GPU capability detection' quote verbatim. source-2.html.gz (Slashdot, archive_fallback, sha256 verified) confirms Valve is funding Collabora's RADV Windows port and that CS2 has been demonstrated, and that a stable interface or compatibility shim will be needed — but does NOT contain the 'shared codebase across platforms, easier debugging and experimentation, faster turnaround on fixes' phrase the article's 'What We Know' section attributes to it as being reported 'in the same words' as XDA. This is a misattribution: only source-3.html.gz (XDA Developers) actually carries that exact phrase (confirmed verbatim: 'shared codebase across platforms, easier debugging and experimentation, faster turnaround on fixes, and a path for the community...'). source-4.html.gz (Open Source For You) confirms the User-Mode Driver (UMD)/WDDM2 framing and the wddm2-pdd-re tool name verbatim. No suspicious_patterns were flagged in manifest.json for any of the 5 sources (all null) — no prompt-injection content found, none reported.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Aside from the single misattributed Slashdot citation noted above, claims trace correctly to their cited sources. In isolation this would be a corrections-note-level issue (a wrong outlet cited for a real, elsewhere-verified quote), not disqualifying on its own.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; consistent with editorial policy.
editor_notes.originality: REJECT-triggering: this submission covers the exact same event as the article published minutes earlier from PR #2108, 'Valve-Sponsored Collabora Effort Ports Mesa's Open-Source RADV Vulkan Driver to Windows, Already Running Counter-Strike 2' (src/content/articles/2026-08/03-valve-sponsored-collabora-effort-ports-mesas-open-source-radv-vulkan-driver-to-windows-already-running-counter-strike-2.md, published 2026-08-03T15:29:35Z, ~46 seconds before this submission's own timestamp of 2026-08-03T15:30:21Z). Both articles report: Valve funding Collabora's RADV-to-Windows port; the milestone of launching Counter-Strike 2 via the -vulkan flag; the prior work by Faith Ekstrand at XDC 2024 and her wddm2-pdd-re tool; removal of the WSL dependency; the same specific technical improvements (sparse bindings, tessellation, task shaders, dynamic GPU property querying); the RX 7900 XT vs RX 7800 XT architecture-mismatch hang; the MSVC enum-signedness compiler bug; the D3DKMT private-data/no-backward-compatibility risk; the need for either a documented AMD kernel interface or a compatibility shim; the 'up to 3x' zero-copy performance estimate; and the same Analysis conclusion (this reflects Valve's long-running investment in the open-source Linux graphics stack behind SteamOS/Steam Deck). This submission's only additions are three extra outlets (Slashdot, XDA Developers, Open Source For You) that themselves just re-report the same Collabora blog post and Linuxiac coverage the published article already cites directly — no new facts, no new developments, no new angle. There is no honest corrections note that could be filed against the published article to 'merge in' this submission's value, because it isn't a correction of anything — it is the same story with different secondary citations. Under the skill's Step 5 criteria this is a REJECT: 'The exact same story was already published' / 'covers the same news with no new information or angle.'
